infosec.title: Security incident on hex.pm
infosec.summary: An attacker ran commands on six hex.pm web servers by sending unauthenticated Erlang-term request bodies containing fake Elixir structs, which got past Plug.Crypto.non_executable_binary_to_term. When Sentry logged the resulting error, inspect triggered a gadget chain through Ecto's DynamicExpr and a DBConnection.Stream :log callback that ran attacker-chosen code (CVE-2026-129514; in place since 2016). Hex patched it within 20 minutes and found no tampered packages, but it can't rule out reads of email addresses, password hashes, and 2FA secrets. Users should change their password, reset 2FA, and fetch packages only from repo.hex.pm until the new signing client ships, and Elixir teams should upgrade Ash to 3.38.0 (CVE-2026-124283) and stop decoding untrusted Erlang terms.

infosec.title: North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware
infosec.summary: North Korea's PolinRider campaign has used stolen GitHub tokens to force-push loaders into at least 7,609 repositories. It rewrites commits the developers already made and hides the code after hundreds of spaces in build configs, conftest.py, or VS Code auto-run tasks, so building the project or just opening the folder runs it. The loader reads its JavaScript stage and its C2 address from Ethereum wallet transactions using a "NullReceiver" scheme marked by "helloipbot!!", so taking servers down does nothing, and OpenSourceMalware traced related activity back to February 2025. Developers should block outbound connections to 95.135.181[.]84 and 103.179.142[.]155, check conftest.py, utils packages, and .vscode/tasks.json for unexpected code, and rotate their GitHub tokens if they find it.

infosec.title: Remus Malware Steals Gmail Messages via Fake Google Sheets Extension
infosec.summary: The developer of the Remus infostealer released a version they claim exploits a zero-day in Gmail to steal emails even after a user resets their password. Researchers reverse-engineered the infostealer and said it installs a malicious Google Chrome extension that masquerades as Google Sheets to steal emails and does not exploit a zero-day. Once active, the extension checks up to ten email accounts for new messages every minute and retrieves them in full, raw format.

infosec.title: Taking over US Treasury subdomains for $3 each
infosec.summary: Intruder researchers claimed 28 AWS Elastic IP addresses that matched dangling DNS records, including five US Treasury subdomains: ftp, irssearch, pcp, rdgw, and ww5.treasury.gov. They allocated and released 450,000 IPs in 48 hours, at a reported cost of $3 per valid takeover. Control of the IP lets an attacker serve content on the subdomain, obtain a TLS certificate, run phishing, capture credentials sent by old automations, and potentially receive cookies scoped to the parent domain. AWS restricted the researchers' account after 48 hours, but transferring the IP to another account in the same organization still worked. AWS said it has no plans to change its approach.

infosec.title: OEMpocalypse Part 2: Rooting Samsung Flagships via Knox DualDAR
infosec.summary: A zero-permission app can root Galaxy S23 and bootloader-locked S26 devices by calling DualDAR's relayAsync. That call forwards commands to a background thread running as system_server, which bypasses the UID check and allows a LOAD_CLIENT_LIBRARY command to execute native code in the dualdard crypto daemon. From there, a page use-after-free in the /dev/dd driver leaves freed memory mapped into userspace, and the chain uses it to corrupt pipe_buffer structures for kernel read/write, disable SELinux, bypass RKP by patching a library in the page cache, and turn off DEFEX. Samsung fixed both bugs in its August and September 2026 updates (CVE-2026-21102). Since Calif's static analysis suggests other Galaxy S and Z models are affected as well, fleet admins should use MDM to require at least the September 2026 patch level.

It combines 122 YAML checks, Praetorian's nerva fingerprinter, and offline NVD and CISA KEV matching with live alerts for evil-twin SSIDs, PoE swaps, and firewall drift. It's a strong option for homelab and small-office UniFi setups, though the maintainers say it is built mostly with AI agents and doesn't accept pull requests, so heavy users should review its code before giving it an API key and access across VLANs.

infosec.title: Linux C2 from Scratch 0x01: Virtualising Your Malware
infosec.summary: The emp3r0r author's second lesson builds a RISC-V (RV32IMA) interpreter that runs BOF payloads as guest code inside a 64 MiB read-write arena, so the payload is never mapped executable and the mmap(PROT_EXEC) and anonymous RX region signals that EDR and eBPF probes look for disappear. The guest reaches the host only through a syscall gate that checks every pointer, and the cost is speed: payloads run orders of magnitude slower than native code. As the author admits, the detection surface shifts rather than disappears: the interpreter is still an anonymous executable .so, and the short-lived arena and the gate's unusual syscall mix can all be fingerprinted.

design.title: Baskerville: The Typeface That Was Too Perfect for Its Time
design.summary: John Baskerville revolutionized eighteenth-century typography by developing a typeface with pronounced stroke contrast, refined serifs, and vertical stress, supported by innovations in ink, paper, and printing techniques. Initially criticized by English readers for its excessive sharpness, Baskerville eventually became an influential transitional serif, inspiring numerous revivals, including Zuzana Licko's Mrs Eaves. Its longstanding association with scholarly publishing and established institutions gives the typeface a sense of authority, with a 2012 experiment even suggesting that it can influence readers' perceived credibility of written statements.

design.title: Can AI Generate Good Designs from Raw User Data?
design.summary: AI-generated designs met 77.9% of scorecard criteria from synthesized findings and recommendations, versus 69.5% from raw user comments, an 8.4-point gap. Raw comments describe problems but rarely say what to build, while synthesis adds the interpretation and design decisions AI tools struggle to make alone. Teams should not assume raw research data is enough context, and the data here was small and cleaner than typical feedback.

design.title: Designers, Get Your Hands Dirty Again
design.summary: Product designers who have risen to the point of barely designing, their days lost to meetings and decisions, may face a rough few years.

design.title: Check out this beautiful wallpaper to celebrate the opening of the latest Apple Store
design.summary: Apple has released an exclusive wallpaper for iPhone, iPad, and Mac to celebrate the December 10 opening of Apple Kukatpally in Hyderabad, its seventh retail store in India.

design.title: Inside the AI Software Factory: Where Accessibility is Won or Lost
design.summary: Accessibility has to be built into AI software factories at every stage, the way privacy and security are, or it brings risk, cost, and rework.

marketing.title: Give Viktor a goal, not a ticket
marketing.summary: You know what the page should say. Then it becomes a ticket, and the ticket waits. Viktor Code skips the queue. Viktor is the AI employee who already knows your customers, your metrics and your brand. Now he writes code too. Give him the goal, like "launch the spring offer." He does both halves: the page, the form and the tracking, then the email, the ads and the results report. Coding agents know your repo. Viktor knows your company. Give Viktor your first goal

marketing.title: Google's Advice for AI Overview Citations is Ordinary SEO
marketing.summary: Google says optimizing for AI Overviews and AI Mode is still traditional SEO, relying on indexed pages with accurate and up-to-date content rather than tactics like rewriting for AI or adding llms.txt files. However, ranking highly in organic search doesn't guarantee AI citations. Ahrefs found only 37.1% of cited pages ranked in Google's organic top 10. SEO teams need to track which pages AI answers actually reference.

marketing.title: Non-Branded Traffic Is Declining. Branded Traffic Is Coming Down With It
marketing.summary: B2B organic search is becoming more reliant on branded traffic, but that does not mean branded demand is growing. Across 34 B2B websites, non-branded clicks fell 35% year over year, while branded clicks fell 19%, making branded traffic a larger share of a shrinking organic channel. Generic informational content is becoming less reliable as a traffic source because AI search can answer many queries without sending users to websites. B2B marketers should invest more in product pages, comparisons, pricing, customer proof, and other high-intent content while building brand visibility across reviews, communities, and third-party sources. Organic performance also needs broader measurement beyond clicks, including AI visibility, brand recommendations, buyer consideration, and revenue.

marketing.title: Editing workflow for 94 SEM landing pages
marketing.summary: AI was used to rewrite 94 paid search landing pages while keeping quality under human control. The work started with writing rules and client-approved messaging to guide the drafts. AI then tailored each page to its target search intent and campaign goals. Every draft went through source-based fact-checking and a 10-role review panel before the original and revised versions were compared by hand.

marketing.title: The UX Behind a Notification Dot
marketing.summary: A subtle notification badge can encourage account creation more effectively than an immediate pop-up because it sparks curiosity without interrupting browsing. The badge works best when it offers a low-commitment reason to click, such as order tracking, saved preferences, or faster checkout based on the visitor's activity. However, sending visitors to a generic login prompt undermines the experience by asking for an account before they understand its value. Test three approaches: no notification, an entrance pop-up, and a persistent badge tied to visitor activity. Measure login starts, account completions, add-to-cart rates, and purchases to see which approach builds customer relationships without hurting conversions.

marketing.title: How Brands Are Winning With Boomers
marketing.summary: Brands targeting boomers are finding growth by tailoring their creative, media mix, and purchasing experience to an underserved audience rather than trying to appeal to younger consumers. Skechers markets hands free shoes through familiar personalities like Martha Stewart, while Boarderie uses calmer Meta ads focused on sending gifts to distant family members after discovering women 65 and older were its largest buyer group. Laura Geller brings QVC-style live shopping to TikTok Shop through 18 to 20 hours of weekly livestreams and more than 20,000 affiliates. Frøya Organics concentrates its skincare advertising on Facebook and Instagram rather than chasing TikTok trends.

marketing.title: Plaid built $382K in pipeline from one TLDR placement
marketing.summary: Close Q4 with proof. TLDR reaches 8 million tech readers across 14 newsletters. Book a Q4 campaign .

marketing.title: 7 steps to building your own website with AI
marketing.summary: Use Claude Design and Paper to build a website without coding, then host it on Vercel. Start with your website copy and brand assets, including fonts and visual references. Design the homepage first before creating other pages. Connect existing tools like Funnel Gorgeous for bookings and beehiiv for newsletter sign-ups. Ask Claude to help publish the site, configure your domain, and run an SEO/AEO audit.

marketing.title: AI Sentiment Analysis for Brands: How to Track and Improve What AI Says About You
marketing.summary: AI sentiment analysis shows how AI assistants describe your brand, the criticisms buyers encounter, and the strengths they associate with competitors. Track both provoked prompts that test known concerns and unprovoked prompts that reveal opinions AI introduces on its own. Compare sentiment across competitors, products, platforms, and topics, then investigate the cited sources to determine whether negative claims reflect outdated information, factual errors, or genuine product weaknesses. Use those findings to update website content, request corrections from publishers, address product problems, and develop marketing assets such as comparison pages, case studies, ads, landing pages, and sales emails.

marketing.title: Organic Sephora Sale Hauls Show Whether Beauty Marketing is Working
marketing.summary: Repeated creator recommendations can have more impact than a single viral post. AI tools can track which brands and products appear in social videos even when they aren't tagged. Product-level mentions reveal which items drive interest, while sentiment analysis helps distinguish genuine recommendations from negative feedback. Brands can also use these insights to understand differences in shopping preferences across age groups.

marketing.title: Top 5 reasons your content is failing in 2026
marketing.summary: Most failing B2B content tries to appeal to everyone and never asks for the sale. Teams skip choosing a narrow audience and positioning, so posts end up as generic advice readers can already get from AI tools. They publish without a repurposing system, which leads to stop-and-go posting that most abandon within weeks. They also hide their offer and skip outreach to people who are already engaged, which can lose half of potential deals.

marketing.title: Micro drama revenue at $20bn in 2026
marketing.summary: China holds 76% of it, and ads on free apps now make up most of its revenue.

marketing.title: Clickbait is a turn-off for young social media scrollers
marketing.summary: Clickbait reduces engagement and credibility, even when posts contain accurate information.

marketing.title: Tech ad spend continues to grow, but AI industry worries could usher in a slowdown
marketing.summary: US tech ad spend growth is projected to slow to 8% in Q4, and investor worries about AI could slow it further.

founders.title: Close Q4 with proof. Start 2027 ready to scale.
founders.summary: Reach 8 million developers, AI experts, security engineers, and founders across 14 newsletters. Plaid built $382K in pipeline from one placement. Book your Q4 campaign .

founders.title: Auditing Enterprise Network Effects
founders.summary: Software founders often rely on network effects to protect B2B products from AI rivals. Those defenses depend on whether customers contribute proprietary data or features that competitors can recreate cheaply. Equifax's proprietary credit data is harder to reproduce than ZoomInfo's publicly available contacts. AI makes thin marketplace features easier to build, so an app ecosystem like Salesforce AppExchange provides less protection. Networks connecting business partners combine proprietary data with distribution because each customer brings counterparties onto the platform, as Nominal does with hardware test data.

founders.title: Is Jevons Paradox holding?
founders.summary: Cheaper AI models are often expected to push total spending higher as usage grows. OpenRouter's paid token volume grew 44 times this year while total spend grew 7.6 times. Usage kept climbing after early October while spend barely moved, so buyers were getting more output without substantially increasing budgets. Enterprises appeared more cost-conscious than AI-native scale-ups in this paid-usage dataset excluding free models and reseller traffic. Similar slowdowns late in earlier years reversed after new model launches.

founders.title: AI and market research: how I use it and where it still fails
founders.summary: Founders are testing AI tools to speed up market research and cut routine admin work. Marketing agency Parvi records every client meeting so an AI agent can write CRM notes and follow-up tasks from actual conversations. Parvi reports that an AI-assisted audit found a B2B account spending roughly 50% more on LinkedIn than competitors while showing the same people ads about 50 times a quarter. The agency rejects synthetic respondents as a replacement for customer interviews and builds its research around real source material.

founders.title: How To Run Your GTM In 2027 (Do These 9 Things First)
founders.summary: Outbound teams are tempted to point AI agents at thousands of accounts on day one. The founder of an outbound agency first tests each account list and email sequence by hand on 25 similar accounts. Each week he picks about 20 high-signal accounts per client and contacts several people at each one personally. Repeatable steps run as fixed n8n workflows, since sending the same job through an AI model on every run costs far more, by his estimate.

founders.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's community (2 minute form)
founders.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss best practices and the latest AI news. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR. Apply here to join .

founders.title: Introducing Search for Agents
founders.summary: Cloudflare's Search for Agents helps websites set up an AI search without having to manually create and configure it initially. It completes all of the integration work required to get a search endpoint available from the site domain, and it makes sure agents know where to find the index and how to use it. The tool automatically creates an index and exposes APIs that any AI agent can discover and use to search your website, under your domain, all done at the network level. Search for Agents can be enabled using the Cloudflare API or through the zone page dashboard.

founders.title: Introducing Effect UI
founders.summary: Effect UI is a frontend library built on Effect and the Elm Architecture. It provides Components with explicit state transitions and side effects as values. Components are self-contained and can provide their own services and load in their own chunk. If a Component fails, the rest of the app keeps running. Effect UI is currently in public preview.

founders.title: Statista gave up most of its 35 million monthly search users to keep its data away from AI
founders.summary: Publishing free pages for Google search used to bring data companies steady traffic. Statista says it drew about 35 million monthly search users before AI crawlers pulled its data into chatbot answers. Customers questioned paying for access, so Statista put almost everything behind a registration wall and saw search users fall to about 8 million. Some smaller customers left because chatbot answers were sufficient, while its enterprise business is growing. Statista now sells licensed data access through an API and MCP server that connect to customers' AI tools.

founders.title: The 3 Financial Plans You Need for The Year: C-90, C-60 and C-10
founders.summary: A C-60 Plan is one where you have a 60% confidence rate you can hit. This is your base plan. A C-10 plan is a variant of the C-60 plan that you think you can maybe hit - this is the stretch plan. A C-90 plan is used to figure out how long a business' cash can last if the next year is harder than planned. Businesses need to make sure they have enough cash to support the C-90 plan, especially during a tougher economy.

founders.title: Refounding Zapier means answering a lot of hard questions
founders.summary: Zapier should be used together with agents to complete real actions in the tools businesses use.

crypto.title: House committee advances Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill
crypto.summary: H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act, would codify a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile, with federally held bitcoin locked for at least 20 years and proof-of-reserve reporting. The Financial Services Committee approved it 28-21 on a party-line vote in September and sent it to the full House on November 24. The 119th Congress is expected to adjourn within weeks, so passage is unlikely. Polymarket gives a 4% chance of a national bitcoin reserve by year end, down from 60% a year ago.

crypto.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs on track for worst month on record
crypto.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs have recorded $5.39B of net outflows in November, already a record with days left, including $453.1M on Wednesday for a seventh straight outflow day. IBIT led with $329.7M. Spot Ether ETFs lost $68.5M, their ninth straight outflow day, and $1.3B for the month. Bitcoin traded near $60,500 after dipping to about $57,300. Galaxy withdrew its call that the bear market ended in June and now treats a daily close below $58,525 as the start of a move to a lower low.

crypto.title: Eclipse Charts: Next-Gen Quantitative Charting Platform
crypto.summary: Eclipse launched as a quantitative charting platform for crypto traders, pairing proprietary indicators (PerpKit, Trend Oracle, and LLNR) with statistical time-series models including ARIMA, Bayesian Trend, and SARIMA. The platform adds neural network candles (nOHLC and nHA), crypto-native orderflow tools (funding rates, open interest, CVD, liquidations, and orderbook heatmaps), and on-chain token charting to the core indicator stack. Traders write and backtest custom scripts via CharmScript, while Premium subscribers at $129/month gain webhook alerts and API access for automated workflows. Pro runs $59/month with a 7-day trial. A free tier exposes the Bitcoin daily chart with all Pro indicators active without an account.

crypto.title: Taskmarket and Visa let TAP-registered agents earn on paid tasks
crypto.summary: Agents registered with Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol can now compete for paid tasks on Taskmarket, built with Visa, Tempo, and Daydreams Labs. Registration requires linking one Visa card once, which is not charged, and gives the agent a signing key listed in the Visa Agentic Directory. Taskmarket checks the signature on entry and again before payout, and rewards are escrowed and paid in OUSD on Tempo. An agent's first 5 task entries are free, then each costs 0.001 OUSD. Starting Thanksgiving, thousands of dollars of tasks open only to TAP-registered agents will be posted, with examples paying $3 to $7. Visa CLI is for US users, and the setup is a six-step command-line process.

crypto.title: Coldcard Postmortem: Seeds Came From a Software RNG for Five Years
crypto.summary: Coldcard firmware generated wallet seeds from March 2021 through July 30, 2026, with MicroPython's Yasmarang software PRNG instead of the STM32 hardware RNG, leaving about 40 bits (Mk2/Mk3) or 72 bits (Mk4, Mk5, Q) of effective entropy, and attackers began regenerating affected private keys offline on July 29. Galaxy Research counted 1,778.84 BTC stolen from more than 8,600 addresses, and Coinkite has matched 300 loss-related support tickets to about 0.2% of its estimated user base. At least 15 independent reviews between 2021 and 2026 missed the defect, including an AI-assisted review with the OpenAI Cybersecurity Harness that produced 85 candidate findings. Coinkite shipped fixed firmware on July 31 but says updates cannot repair seeds created on affected firmware, and it is still evaluating options to help affected customers.

crypto.title: Beyond Table Stakes: Architectures for Stablecoin Issuance
crypto.summary: Stablecoin issuance has split into four architectures: chain-native primitives (Tempo TIP-20, Base B20, and Solana Token-2022) that move compliance into the protocol, OUSD's mixed setup, white-label platforms like M0, and Paxos's reward-bearing Token V3. OUSD has reached about $983M in supply across four chains since its late-September launch, with 64% on Tempo, using native primitives on Tempo, Base, and Solana, while Bridge built a custom two-layer ERC-20 stack on Ethereum. M0's base token M backs branded stablecoins such as MetaMask's mUSD and has processed over $1B in mints across Solana and 15+ EVM chains, a design PYUSDx copies with PYUSD as the base. Paxos upgraded USDG in place to V3 in 2026, splitting it into a core token plus five facets and paying rewards to distribution partners through onchain payout groups instead of to holders.

crypto.title: How I Got Started with Crypto HFT
crypto.summary: @0xyieldmaxi built a two-person prop trading firm in Switzerland after post-FTX MEV alpha decayed, scaling from fixed-spread quoting on Binance through cross-exchange arbitrage to CEX-DEX arb, which they found highly profitable with thin competition at peak. The actual trading logic ran under 100 lines of code. The bulk of the work was exchange connectivity, WebSocket latency optimization via Avelacom, and fee negotiation across Binance, Bybit, and OKX. A partner split in late 2024 cut PnL, and they missed Hyperliquid while focused on optimizing existing operations, with edge eroding enough to step away by mid-2025. They're returning in 2026, targeting prediction markets and using LLMs to compress the cycle from idea to testable strategy.

crypto.title: Why Tokens Could Be Entering a Decade-Long Bull Market
crypto.summary: Five years of token bear market have flushed out inflated valuations, weak tokens, and capital misallocation. The reversal of those conditions sets up a decade-long secular bull market. This case rests on cheap valuations and disciplined capital, Internet Finance products such as stablecoins and RWAs that work but are hidden by negative industry P&L, and network effects that turn onchain markets into a global bazaar for cheaper capital and better assets. With fewer than 15 funds and under 1,000 serious people left in the industry, there's a "dry forest" where the spark could be GENIUS in January, RWAs reaching critical mass, easier macro liquidity, or a niche industry raising capital onchain.

crypto.title: Aave App draws $60M+ from 5,000+ depositors in under three months
crypto.summary: During its waitlist phase, the Aave App cleared more than 5,000 depositors averaging roughly $12K each, for total balances of $60M to $63M.

crypto.title: Unauthorized party accessed limited Zodia Custody client information
crypto.summary: Zodia Custody, which Standard Chartered is acquiring, said an unauthorized party accessed limited client data after attempts to probe its platform.

crypto.title: MiniPay Card cuts cashback from 5% to 2% on most purchases
crypto.summary: The free Visa card in the MiniPay wallet offered 5% back, up to $100 a month, with no foreign currency fee.

crypto.title: How Much No-KYC Crypto Cards Let You Spend Before Asking for ID
crypto.summary: A review of six no-KYC cards found caps as tight as $10,000 a year on kardpay Core ($29 a year), $5,000 a month on Solcard Virtual per its help center, and $1,000 per non-reloadable Laso card, while Goblin's physical card allows $5,000 a day.

it.title: SAP and planqc Bring Quantum Computing into Business Processes
it.summary: SAP expects quantum computing could become practical for its business software before the decade ends. planqc hardware tests are planned for 2027.

it.title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
it.summary: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners including Dell and Super Micro to temporarily pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. The pause will allow Nvidia to assess whether regional partners are complying with US export requirements. The measure follows a US Commerce Department rule change targeting remote access to Nvidia chips by Chinese companies through data centers in those countries.

it.title: Can small IT teams afford the shift to conversational helpdesks?
it.summary: ServiceNow launched Flow, a conversational AI service desk designed to handle employee IT requests directly within communication platforms like Slack and Microsoft Teams. While proponents highlight potential productivity gains and streamlined workflows, small and mid-sized IT teams face steep pricing models, unpredictable conversational billing, and risks of workflow sprawl or service disruptions.

it.title: AI made self-hosting fun again
it.summary: The integration of AI coding agents into infrastructure management has restored their enthusiasm for self-hosting by significantly reducing routine friction. AI tools make it easier to experiment with unfamiliar technologies like NixOS, automate deployment pipelines with Git, and build custom single-purpose utilities. Consequently, routine maintenance tasks require less manual effort, allowing the author to pursue spontaneous infrastructure projects more frequently.

it.title: Ubuntu on Azure at Ignite 2026: Cobalt 200, Foundry, and managed apps
it.summary: At Microsoft Ignite 2026, Canonical announced broad Ubuntu integrations across Azure services, highlighted by generally available Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines running Arm64 images and Microsoft Foundry Managed Compute using Ubuntu Pro security patches. Additional announcements included new Ubuntu 26.04 LTS foundations for Azure App Service runtimes, two new managed applications on the Azure Marketplace, and public previews for confidential computing, AKS node sizes, and SQL Server 2025 support.

it.title: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026: What we heard in Salt Lake City
it.summary: At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026, discussions focused heavily on AI traffic management and Ingress-NGINX migration paths following the project's retirement. NGINX highlighted migration tools for moving to NGINX Ingress Controller or NGINX Gateway Fabric, and presented new solutions for AI gateway controls, policy-as-code patterns, and MCP agent security. SlashData's enterprise-grade Kubernetes report also revealed that only 38 percent of surveyed enterprises reach enterprise-grade maturity despite widespread production use.

it.title: Can you confidently ship to production from your phone?
it.summary: Developers can ship application bug fixes directly to production from their mobile devices using AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, or Grok. By integrating Expo MCP servers, GitHub, Expo Simulators, and Expo Update, AI agents can diagnose bugs, create pull requests, and verify fixes on cloud simulators. Developers can then deploy verified fixes to users worldwide through over-the-air updates.

it.title: Your Model Is a Dependency
it.summary: Large language models should follow standard software supply chain governance practices to address behavioral drift, transitive dependencies, and security risks. Six core practices include pinning complete model configurations, statistically testing upgrades with McNemar's test, maintaining an AI bill of materials, removing unnecessary agent tool definitions, verifying load provenance, and planning structured exit strategies.

it.title: SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 positions in AI restructuring
it.summary: The cuts would affect approximately 9% of the company's global workforce, though the final total remains subject to ongoing labor negotiations.

it.title: Rotate AWS Keys Stored in easyDNS CP Immediately
it.summary: easyDNS is urging all users who store their AWS keys in the easyDNS control panel for Route53 integration to rotate those keys immediately following reports of key compromises.

hardware.title: TSMC's A14 is ready for design-in with PDK 0.9
hardware.summary: A14 uses second-generation nanosheet transistors with flexible cell types, so designers put fast Boost Cells on critical paths and power-saving Low-Power Cells everywhere else. TSMC claims 50% better energy efficiency and 23% higher logic density than N2P, and a later move to A13 shrinks die area about 6% without changing the design flow.

hardware.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million solar-powered orbital data center satellites, with 100,000 due by November 2035
hardware.summary: SpaceX has been authorized to launch a constellation of up to 1 million AI satellites that would link to each other optically and reach Earth through Starlink, with the 1 million count acting as a regulatory ceiling rather than a promised fleet. SpaceX plans to equip them with Nvidia Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs, relying on Starship's falling launch costs to compete with terrestrial datacenter prices

hardware.title: Quick Take: AMD's Helios as a Plug-and-Play AI Appliance Standard
hardware.summary: AMD's Helios combines AMD CPU, GPU, and Ethernet with the ROCm framework in a plug-and-play AI solution using OCP's ORW form factor. Positioned as a competitive alternative to NVIDIA's offerings, AMD focuses on integration and easier software porting from CUDA to ROCm. Though larger cloud providers depend on NVIDIA or custom AI ASICs, smaller providers may leverage Helios's integration for straightforward deployment and operation.

hardware.title: NERC's first standards require data centers of 50 MW or more to share power models and trip settings, after 3.8 GW of Virginia load dropped off the grid at once
hardware.summary: On July 22, Northern Virginia facilities drawing 3,800 MW switched to backup after a routine line fault, spiking frequency and voltage, and at least eight such events have shed 200 to 1,800 MW since 2022. AI training makes it worse, since synchronized GPUs pulse between full power and near idle, and a 100 MW facility swung 10 to 15 MW every 2.5 seconds. Simulations show those pulses can resonate with grid natural frequencies, so NERC also plans ride-through and oscillation criteria next year.

hardware.title: SK hynix to Start 3D DRAM Production in 2031
hardware.summary: SK hynix plans to start mass production of 3D DRAM by 2031, potentially utilizing 100-layer designs based on its current roadmap. The production requires advanced techniques like multi-deck stacking and hybrid bonding, drawing from technology licensed from YMTC. This shift involves completely overhauling SK hynix's DRAM architecture and manufacturing process.

hardware.title: Xpeng says its IRON humanoid will sell at roughly the median price of its EVs
hardware.summary: Xpeng's EVs run from 119,800 to 309,800 yuan (about $18,000 to $44,000), and an executive gave that as the benchmark for the future cost of their humanoid, IRON. IRON carries over 1,500 tactile sensing points, with 76 degrees of freedom and three in-house Turing AI chips. Mass production starts in January. Store trials follow in Q1 2027, and public sales are targeted for Q2. Xpeng wants to sell tens of thousands next year, funded by a $900 million robotics round at a $6.3 billion valuation, while its stock is down 55% this year.

hardware.title: 2 California companies are buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Those companies are actually Chinese-owned, a CBS News investigation reveals
hardware.summary: Nvidia's advanced chips are being sold to US-based companies that are actually Chinese-owned, raising concerns about evading export controls. California companies RiCloud AI and Aivres, linked to Chinese firms, have been involved in questionable dealings, including sales to Southeast Asian firms tied to Chinese tech companies. Nvidia's accounting changes may obscure customer locations, prompting potential Senate investigations into export violations and espionage.

hardware.title: EU delays its vote on bloc-wide approval of Tesla's "hands-off, eyes-on" driver assistance
hardware.summary: The Technical Committee for Motor Vehicles had been expected to vote after skipping two earlier meetings, following the Netherlands' approval in April. Tesla Assisted Driving, renamed from FSD after regulator concerns, can steer, accelerate, and brake, but needs constant driver supervision. About 12 countries have approved it, with Italy the largest, but EU-wide approval takes 15 of 27 states representing 65% of the population, and a rejection would invalidate the national approvals already granted.

hardware.summary: AMD's Radeon RX 9060 XT reached a new GPU frequency world record of 4.837 GHz with liquid nitrogen cooling.

ai.title: Anthropic prepares Google Drive file browser for Claude

The interface will display Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides and allow users to search and filter files. It currently appears as a separate item in Claude's navigation sidebar. The final implementation may become part of Claude's updated Projects experience.

ai.title: OpenAI may be in cost control mode
ai.summary: OpenAI's Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 updates received criticism for reduced performance, as both models show significant reductions in reasoning and output tokens. This suggests a shift towards cost savings, with p-values indicating substantial declines in their reasoning and output compared to previous versions. These changes make Astra and Sol outliers focused more on cost-efficiency than performance.

ai.title: Measuring RSI
ai.summary: Neither compute allocation nor human intervention measures whether an AI training algorithm improved. Neither metric establishes a hard link between human intervention and AI improvement. Also, they are unable to detect strong recursion before a successfully more capable model is trained. Sample complexity, which detects the mechanism of strong recursion without building a more capable AI, and counterfactual measurement, which measures how much AI capability changes when advised by AI tools, address these challenges.

ai.title: Your Model Is a Dependency
ai.summary: The large language model (LLM) you choose to use is a dependency. Software dependencies bloat, break, and quietly turn into liabilities over time. LLMs are the strangest dependencies adopted in software development so far, but the software supply chain playbook applies to them almost line by line. Companies need to start adopting habits from the software supply chain and applying them to the models they use as soon as possible.

ai.title: From Model Compression to Looped Transformers
ai.summary: Model layers are not all equally sensitive to compression. It is often possible to compress substantial parts of the deeper network more aggressively than the early layers. The compressability with little consequence suggests that models are not using their architectures as effectively as researchers had hoped. Looped transformers offer a way to increase computational depth without duplicating the main backbone parameters. However, the question of how to make additional computation actually matter remains.

ai.title: Plato's Key
ai.summary: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that neural networks converge toward a shared representation of reality. Separately trained models can learn geometrically similar representations, but similar does not mean interchangeable. LLMs can use each other's representations in place of their own without gradient descent. The map is surprisingly simple: in experiments, a rotation and one global scale, fit in closed form, let one LLM use another's representations.

ai.title: LayerStream: faster MoE fine-tuning on fewer or cheaper GPUs
ai.summary: Nebius' LayerStream training engine keeps optimizer state and saved activations in host memory and streams each layer's working state through the GPU only when that layer runs. On 16 H200 GPUs, it finished a pass over a 25.8M-token dataset in 7.1 minutes instead of 22.4, with 3.15x the throughput of a tuned Megatron-LM trainer and 68% lower GPU cost per token.

ai.title: Why I'm Bullish on MCP for 2027
ai.summary: MCP is evolving, with entities like Linear, Notion, and Atlassian using it for significant tool management, showing robust growth in traffic and tool handling. Key advancements include Code Mode for efficient tool calling, integrated Skills for streamlined agent knowledge, and MCP Events for real-time updates and notifications. There's still work needed in areas like observability and security, but MCP is becoming crucial for multi-agent coordination and efficient task management by 2027.

ai.title: Do scale-dependent algorithms cut against a software intelligence explosion?
ai.summary: Scale-dependent algorithms will cut against a software-only intelligence explosion. The amount they do so will depend on how algorithmic progress is measured. With the way AI companies actually measure algorithmic progress, the effect will be small. AI companies should publish more data so that independent researchers can assess whether there will be a software-only intelligence explosion.
